Players of the game from Ohio State’s 19-15 win over Indiana

Players of the game from Ohio State’s 19-15 win over Indiana

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:24
Instaread

A number of Buckeyes played a key role in Ohio State snapping Indiana’s 22-game winning streak on Saturday in Bloomington

by Brett Ludwiczak
Oct 18, 2026, 11:15 AM EDT
00Comments

Saturday’s game between Ohio State and Indiana in Bloomington was a slugfest.

Julian Sayin left Memorial Stadium in a sling after suffering an apparent shoulder injury in the fourth quarter. According to head coach Ryan Day, it is not yet known how long Sayin will be sidelined, but the quarterback is expected to miss several weeks.

The Buckeyes and Hoosiers combined for just 23 points when they met in December in the Big Ten Championship Game, and their latest meeting followed a similar script. After many twists and turns in Bloomington, the Buckeyes were able to grit out a 19-15 win to snap the 22-game winning streak of the Hoosiers after Nick Marsh came down with a foot out of bounds on what would have been the game-winning touchdown for Indiana.

In a contest that was so closely contested, there were a number of Buckeyes who stood out with their play on Saturday. There are some Ohio State players on both sides of the football who deserve recognition for their contributions to the winning effort against Indiana.

Jeremiah Smith

The stats the Ohio State wide receiver put up against Indiana weren’t anywhere close to what Smith did against Illinois or Iowa, but what the junior still demanded plenty of attention.

A prime example came on Bo Jackson’s receiving touchdown right before halftime, when Smith had multiple Hoosiers covering him, allowing Jackson to have enough room to catch a screen pass and find the end zone on fourth down.

Icon Sportswire via Getty Images

Smith also had a massive impact on a fourth down play in the second half. With just under 13 minutes left in the fourth quarter, Ohio State faced a 4th-and-1. Instead of running the football, Julian Sayin decided to air it out, finding Smith in the end zone for a touchdown that pushed Ohio State’s lead to 19-7.

Smith would finish with four catches for 68 yards and the one touchdown.

Isaiah West

After seeing more carries in the second half of his freshman season last year, Isaiah West was expected to compete with Bo Jackson for the starting running back job this year. Instead, Florida transfer Ja’Kobi Jackson has been the back who has shared carries with Jackson in 2026.

Entering this week’s game, West had just 22 carries for 80 yards. With Ja’Kobi Jackson out injured and Legend Bey still not fully trusted by the coaching staff, West’s number was called more against the Hoosiers.

The sophomore had some important runs on Saturday, finishing with 45 yards on the ground on six carries. The numbers may not look like all that much but the output could energize West and give Ohio State another running back they can count on in the second half of the season.

Jay Timmons

The talented freshman defensive back had missed the last two games because of injury, but Timmons looked fully healthy on Saturday against the Hoosiers. Not only did Timmons make seven tackles in the victory, early in the third quarter he forced the first fumble by Indiana in over 1,400 offensive snaps.

There was a point in the game where it felt like Timmons was everywhere on defense. While there was times when the Buckeyes defensive struggled to keep the passing attack from the Hoosiers from making some noise, the play of Timmons helped to keep Indiana from turning drives that reached Ohio State territory into touchdowns.

Earl Little Jr.

The player who ended up recovering the fumble forced by Timmons early in the third quarter was fellow defensive back Earl Little Jr. The former Alabama and Florida State safety continued the strong start to his first season with the Buckeyes with a team-high eight tackles.

Icon Sportswire via Getty Images

While the fumble recovery was Little’s highlight of the game, he also did set the tone with a pass breakup intended for Charlie Becker on third down early in the first quarter.

Entering the bye week, Little has a team-high 38 tackles and has been credited with four passes defensed through seven games.

Connor Hawkins

To say special teams have been lacking during Ryan Day’s tenure as head coach would be an understatement. When Hawkins came on to attempt two short field goals on Saturday, Buckeye Nation was having flashbacks to Jayden Fielding miss a chip shot in the Big Ten Championship Game in December.

To Hawkins’ credit, he nailed both kicks when his number was called, which is more than Indiana kicker Nico Radicic can say. In the end, Hawkins making his kicks and Radicic missing his ended up being the difference in the game.

Had Radicic made his two field goals, then it wouldn’t have mattered that Marsh stepped out of bounds in the end zone late in the fourth quarter.
